article_title: Ricursive Intelligence Releases Ripple-65B Preview, an Apache 2.0 Dense Model That Reports a Terminal-Bench 2.1 Lead Over Selected U.S. Open Models

content_preview.title: Ricursive Intelligence Releases Ripple-65B Preview, an Apache 2.0 Dense Model That Reports a Terminal-Bench 2.1 Lead Over Selected U.S. Open Models
content_preview.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a 65B dense model listed under Apache 2.0, reporting 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1; VentureBeat notes mixed results elsewhere and conflicting figures.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Ricursive Intelligence has released Ripple-65B Preview, a dense Transformer with 65 billion parameters, and the [model card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview) lists its license as Apache 2.0. The company reports a Terminal-Bench 2.1 score of 80.52 for the model, ahead of four other U.S. open-weight models it compares against. [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/technology/ex-googlers-new-apache-2-0-model-ripple-65b-preview-claims-the-u-s-open-c...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article (994 words, within the 400-1200 range). Separates what the model card states from what VentureBeat reports, labels benchmark figures as Ricursive's own, and carries VentureBeat's caveats (selected competitors, conflicting figures, non-comparable cost accounting). Title is 147 characters (under the 150 limit). Title, summary and lead are each backed by a cited source.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three stored snapshots (manifest: status 200 for all, suspicious_patterns null for all). source-0.html.gz (Hugging Face model card): confirmed 65B parameter dense Transformer, 12T tokens, 1Mi (1,048,576 tokens) context, d_model 5120, 80 layers, BF16 and NVFP4 instruct plus BF16 base, 'Our Preview release has gone through relatively light posttraining, with a focus on agentic coding.', 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1 ahead of Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4), Thinking Machines Inkling 975B (63.8), NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (56.4); SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard 79.1 vs 76.5 for Beam; DeepSWE 1.1 44.3 vs 60.0 Muse Spark; SWE-bench Verified 76.5 vs 81.6 Beam; GPQA Diamond 85.2 vs 87.0-90.6; Terminus 2 / OpenCode harness statements; in-house eval flow for missing evals; 'Replicating benchmark scores has been challenging' and 'a best-effort attempt at a fair comparison'; DGX Spark and 250 tok/s on 2xB200 batch=8 claims; 65B active vs 23B for Beam. The card contains no mention of Artificial Analysis or any independent or third-party evaluation of Ripple. source-1.html.gz (LICENSE): heading 'Apache License, Version 2.0, January 2004'. I additionally diffed the raw LICENSE (via the Hugging Face raw endpoint) against the canonical text at apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt: identical apart from a trailing newline; no additions, restrictions or NOTICE; the card metadata also reads license: apache-2.0. source-2.html.gz (VentureBeat, Carl Franzen, November 4, 2026; the snapshot is the full article text, not a bot-check page): confirmed the quoted 'applies to selected U.S. competitors and tests', 'a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model that powers our AI chip design platform', 'A broader coding crown would overstate that evidence.', 'is not a directly comparable accounting disclosure from both companies.', 'no revenue or monthly-user threshold requiring a separate commercial agreement' and 'do not settle'; AlphaChip founders, $300 million Series A in January led by Lightspeed at $4 billion; API partners Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter with Fireworks soon; $0.20/$0.60 per million tokens with cached input $0.05 and 16,384-token context, scoped to the November 4 status check; Together and Fireworks rate language; $32 million development cost, 1.4 million rollouts, roughly 70 times fewer than Reflection, Reflection's more than 100 million rollouts over four weeks; margin of approximately 0.4 percentage points; Reflection's 77.2 and 44.4 Beam figures described as separate vendor evaluations; 52.3 and 2.0 in the model card versus 72.4 and 39.6 in the launch graphic. All 10 quoted strings in the article match their sources verbatim. Independent-source count: 1 of 3 (VentureBeat; the model card and LICENSE are the subject's own pages). Not required for News.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All figures, dates and names verified. Independent-evaluation statement checked against BOTH sources and holds: VentureBeat's phrase 'two third-party benchmarks' describes the benchmarks, not an evaluation of Ripple; its only 'independently' (Reflection reporting rollouts) concerns Reflection; it cites no Artificial Analysis, OpenRouter-measured or other third-party measurement of Ripple's quality, and the card cites none either. The model-card discrepancy was verified through the Hugging Face commit history (the card, not the stored memory, is the evidence): revisions through 240d5966 (Nov 4) list SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard as 52.3 for Muse Spark and 2.0 for Inkling, matching VentureBeat; commit 30cb3b0e (Nov 6, 03:01 UTC, 'Update README.md') changed the row to 72.4 and 39.6. The article's statement that the card may have changed after VentureBeat's review is therefore correct (it also correctly says the Herald did not see the earlier version); the 79.1 figure was in every revision. Pricing is scoped to VentureBeat's November 4 check. The internal links were opened: the Kimi K3.1 Pro article (license with a separate-agreement condition for Model-as-a-Service businesses above 20 million US dollars in revenue) and the Mistral Large 4 article (modified MIT license requiring a commercial license for Model-as-a-Service operators) are described accurately, and the new article does not repeat the flawed statements for which corrections were filed on those two articles (no claim about absence of independent replication carried over from them; here the claim was verified against the sources). No relative dates. The three non-allowlisted sources the writer cross-read (Ricursive blog, OpenRouter, Together AI, Reflection post) are not cited and the article relies only on the three allowlisted sources (huggingface.co and venturebeat.com are both in config/source_allowlist.txt).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Every performance and efficiency claim is attributed to Ricursive or VentureBeat; the title uses 'Reports' and 'Selected', in line with VentureBeat's qualification.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Herald article on Ripple or Ricursive in src/content/articles. Related to, but not duplicating, the Kimi K3.1 Pro and Mistral Large 4 licensing articles (linked in the article and added to related_articles in article-meta).
concerns: Minor omission, not an error: the model card's table has a second Terminal-Bench 2.1 row (Terminus 2 harness) in which Ripple scores 80.5 against 78.7 for Muse Spark Open and 70.8 for Beam, and the card says scores were universally lower with the official harness except for Muse Spark Open. The article reports only the 'self-reported' row's figures and does not state that the card's own harness caveat applies to Terminal-Bench. The headline lead (80.52 vs the four listed models) is accurate as stated.

Minor: the article says VentureBeat located no Ripple-specific public rate for Together AI or Fireworks AI; VentureBeat's wording for Fireworks is 'No confirmed Ripple-specific rate located' and it notes a generic Fireworks tier. Acceptable paraphrase, scoped to the check date.

Minor: the article's final Licensing sentence says the Herald has not independently reviewed the full license text for obligations; this review did compare the file with the canonical Apache 2.0 text and found it unmodified. The hedge is conservative, not wrong.
Pattern scanner: no suspicious_patterns matches in any snapshot, so no override was needed.
recommendations: When a model card reports the same benchmark under two harnesses, state both rows or the card's harness caveat.
Cross-check the model-card revision history when a secondary source reports figures that differ from the current card.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed coverage of a vendor-reported open-weight release, with every specific traced to the three allowlisted sources and no claims resting on non-allowlisted material. Approved as written. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid release coverage for developers and model evaluators; the lead is a vendor-reported benchmark claim with no independent measurement yet.
